content: Hello everyone, I am a mathematician working in algebraic geometry. I am interested in learning lean with a goal of contributing to the formalization of basics related to the (pro-)etale topology. A few years ago I have contributed a tiny bit to mathlib, but I consider myself a newbie. I am interested in working on a formalization of the henselization of pairs (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EM7), which I think could be accessible using orthogonal factorization systems. As a small step for this, I have worked out a file that contains some basics regarding unique lifting properties. I will immediately acknowledge that this file was coauthored using AI, which I have read is regarded with suspicion in the community. So before considering to starting a PR on mathlib with this, I wanted to bring it up here. Thanks for any comments!

First, I should mention that I am really not an expert in topology, and I am still very much a beginner when it comes to the pro-étale side of things, so I may be missing the right conceptual connection here.

I had a look at what is already available in mathlib around Hensel's lemma. There is a p-adic version in Mathlib.NumberTheory.Padics.Hensel, and more abstract infrastructure around henselian rings in Mathlib.RingTheory.Henselian.

One thing that seems relevant for a more elementary Hensel lifting argument is that mathlib already has Polynomial.eval_add_of_sq_eq_zero in Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Taylor. It gives essentially

f(x + y) = f(x) + f'(x) * y

when y^2 = 0.

This is exactly the first-order Taylor step one uses when lifting a root from mod p^(e-1) to mod p^e, by taking y = k * p^(e-1). As far as I can tell, what seems to be missing is a packaged elementary “one-step Hensel lift” theorem in terms of congruences, even though most of the ingredients are already there.

I don't know if it helps, but perhaps you can see better than I do whether this existing Taylor/Henselian infrastructure connects naturally to the lifting-property approach you have in mind for henselization of pairs.

@Daniel Sautot yes, what you refer to is an instance of the statement that any local ring that is complete with respect to its $\mathfrak m$-adic topology is Henselian (already in mathlib https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.html#IsAdicComplete.henselianRing). The henselization of pairs that I refer to is a bit more general, given a pair consisting of a ring $A$ and an ideal $I$, it produces a new ring $A^h$, that is Henselian with respect to $I^h := I A^h$.
(You can use double-$ to get LaTeX rendering)
